question: Which of the following organisations was established in 1906?
solution:
The correct answer is __**All India Muslim League**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **All India Muslim League** was established in the year **1906**.
 
• The organization was formed in **Dhaka, British India** (now in Bangladesh).
 
• Its main aim was to represent the interests of the **Muslim diaspora in India** and to promote loyalty to the British government.
 
• The League played a crucial role in the creation of **Pakistan** in 1947.
 
• Prominent leaders associated with the Muslim League include **Sir Aga Khan, Nawab Salimullah, and Mohammad Ali Jinnah**.
 
• The foundation of the League was a response to the political and socio-economic challenges faced by Muslims in India during the British colonial period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha**__

 __
 
• The **Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha** was founded in **1915**.
 
• It is a right-wing Hindu nationalist organization in India.
 
• The organization was founded to protect the rights and interests of the Hindu community.
 
• Prominent leaders include **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar**.
 
 
 
• **Servants of India Society**__
 __
 
• The **Servants of India Society** was founded by **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** in **1905**.
 
• It aimed to train national missionaries for the service of India.
 
• The organization focused on social and economic reforms.
 
 
 
• **Parsi Religious Reform Association**__
 
 
• The **Parsi Religious Reform Association** was founded in **1851**.
 
• It aimed at reforming the Zoroastrian religion and community practices.
 
• The association was part of the larger socio-religious reform movements in India during the 19th century.
